articles.title: Falinge Park High School celebrates Artsmark Week with students
articles.excerpt: Falinge Park High School recently hosted an Artsmark Celebration Week, recognising the contributions of students in Years 7 to 10. The event took place over the past week and aimed to highlight the importance of cultural education for all learners.
articles.content_html:
Falinge Park High School recently hosted an Artsmark Celebration Week, recognising the contributions of students in Years 7 to 10. The event aimed to highlight the importance of cultural education for all learners.

During the celebration, students participated in discussions about why access to high-quality cultural education is essential. They articulated their thoughts on the significance of such education in their development.

The school commended the students for their active participation and engagement throughout the week, fostering a deeper understanding of cultural education's role in personal and academic growth.

Falinge Park High School is committed to providing a rich cultural education experience, aligning with the Artsmark framework, which encourages schools to deliver high-quality arts and cultural experiences.

articles.title: Students trained as Rochdale Creative Health Advocates at Falinge Park High School
articles.excerpt: Students from various schools participated in training to become Creative Health Advocates, aimed at promoting health and wellbeing in the community.
articles.content_html:
Students from multiple schools participated in training last week to become Rochdale Creative Health Advocates at Falinge Park High School. The initiative aims to empower young people to promote health and wellbeing within their communities.

The training focused on equipping students with skills to advocate for health-related issues, encouraging them to take an active role in improving the wellbeing of their peers and families. This programme is part of a broader effort to engage youth in community health initiatives.

Falinge Park High School has been instrumental in facilitating this training, providing resources and support to ensure students are well-prepared for their roles as advocates. The school aims to foster a sense of responsibility and leadership among its students.

This initiative aligns with ongoing efforts to enhance community health in Rochdale, encouraging young people to contribute positively to their environment. The next steps include further training sessions and opportunities for students to engage with local health projects.

articles.title: Full house for National Emergency Briefing screening in Falinge
articles.excerpt: A community screening of the National Emergency Briefing attracted a full room in Falinge, with Rochdale councillors Tricia Ayrton and Shah Wazir joining residents for the event and discussion afterwards.
articles.content_html:
A community screening of the National Emergency Briefing attracted a full room in Falinge, with two Rochdale Council portfolio holders joining residents for the event and subsequent discussion.

Organisers have thanked everyone who attended the screening, saying it was encouraging to see such a strong turnout for the film and the conversation which followed.

Rochdale Borough Council portfolio holders Councillor Tricia Ayrton and Councillor Shah Wazir were among those attending.

Organisers thanked both councillors for remaining after the screening to listen to residents, take part in discussions and consider how the issues raised by the film could be discussed more widely.

They said the councillors left the event with a plan to help ensure the film and its message reach a broader audience.

The National Emergency Briefing brings together scientists, campaigners and public figures to discuss climate change and the risks they believe the UK faces, with contributors associated with the project including environmental campaigner Chris Packham.

The Falinge event gave residents an opportunity not only to watch the presentation together but to discuss its arguments and what they could mean at a local level.

Following the strong turnout, another community screening has already been arranged.

The next screening will take place on Thursday 4 September at 6pm, giving residents who were unable to attend the latest event another opportunity to see the film and join the discussion.

Organisers thanked residents, guests and councillors for supporting the event and helping create what they described as an important community conversation.
